name: The Church App
version: v4 · 2026-11-08 · practice church, and the two closing steps every script has · store step: free
verified: 2026-11-08 · driven against church-demo: the home screen, the demo notice, the sermon notes panel and its two tabs, the Questions section, the prayer wall and its three seeded requests, the empty-send refusal, sending a request properly, and the Give button going nowhere. NOT driven from the container: adding a note and the verse pickup (steps 5 to 7) — those steps ask the tester to say what they saw rather than asserting it.
intro:
✅ THIS IS A PRACTICE CHURCH. Grace Harbor Church is invented — the sermons, the people, the events and the prayers in it are all made up. Nothing you do here reaches anybody.

That is new. Until today this test ran on a real church's live app in America, and you were told not to touch half of it in case a real prayer request landed on a real desk. So half of it has never been tested by anyone. This time you can use all of it — send a prayer request, press the giving button, poke at everything.

If you type anything, make it up. You never need to put your own name, your own family or anything true into a test.

You will write sermon notes and find them again, try the prayer wall properly, look at giving and events, work offline, and switch the app to dark.

steps.do: Open the app. Near the bottom of the Home screen, find the tip that starts "Add to Home Screen" and tap "GOT IT".
steps.see: The tip goes away. At the top there is a grey note with a 👋, then the latest message — "Anchored · Week 3 · A living hope", 1 Peter 1:3–9, Dan Whitfield — and events under it.
steps.tip: If you see a church you recognise instead of Grace Harbor, stop and tell us — you are in the wrong app.

steps.do: Read the grey note at the very top, the one beside the 👋. Then, without looking back at it, say in your own words what it told you.
steps.see: Your answer is the test here, not the app's. It should be clear to you that this church is not real and that nothing you do reaches anybody. If it was not clear, say so — that is a real finding.

steps.do: Scroll down the Home screen to "Discussion guide" and tap "📝 My notes on this message".
steps.see: A "📝 Sermon Notes" panel opens with two tabs, "🎙 During" and "✨ After". Lower down there is "✍️ My notes" with an empty box.

steps.do: Tap the box under "✍️ My notes" — it says "What stood out to you…" — and type exactly this: Grandma's favorite verse is Acts 2:4
steps.see: Your words are in the box.

steps.do: Tap "Add" next to the box.
steps.see: Say what happens. We expect your note to appear under the box with a • in front of it, and the box to empty ready for the next one — but this is the first time this test has run on the practice church and nobody has watched this step on a real phone. If something else happens, that is exactly what we need.

steps.do: With the box now empty, tap "Add" again.
steps.see: Nothing is added. There is still only your one note.

steps.do: At the top of the panel, tap "✨ After".
steps.see: Under “📜 Scriptures in this sermon” the app should have picked “Acts 2:4” out of the note you typed and made a button of it. Say whether it did. Under “Questions to take home” there are numbered questions, each with a box to answer in — that part we have checked.

steps.do: Tap the "📖 Acts 2:4" button.
steps.see: Say what happens. It may open the verse, or it may do nothing because this is a practice copy. Either is worth writing down — we want to know which one you got.

steps.do: Answer the first question in its box, in a sentence. Make the answer up — it does not have to be true.
steps.see: Your answer stays in the box.

steps.do: Scroll down to "📤 Share" and tap "Share this sermon". Then cancel the share without sending.
steps.see: Your phone's own share menu opens, with the sermon title, the questions and the verses ready to send. Nothing is sent when you cancel.

steps.do: Tap the ✕ at the top right of the Sermon Notes panel.
steps.see: The panel closes and you are back on the Home screen.

steps.do: Tap "Watch" in the bar at the bottom.
steps.see: The Messages list opens, newest at the top, with buttons for each series: All, Anchored, Standalone, Lifelines, The Good Shepherd. The top message is "Anchored: Week 3 · A living hope".

steps.do: Tap the message at the top of the list.
steps.see: The message opens, and under "My notes" the box already holds the note you wrote: Grandma's favorite verse is Acts 2:4

steps.do: Tap "Back" at the top left.
steps.see: You are back on the Messages list, and the top message now carries a "Notes saved" label.

steps.do: Pull the page down to reload it.
steps.see: The app comes back on the Messages list and the top message still says "Notes saved". Your note survived the reload.

steps.do: Tap "Prayer" in the bar at the bottom.
steps.see: "Let's pray together" at the top, a grey line saying this is a demo and nothing is sent anywhere, then THREE requests already on the wall — from Maria, from Anonymous, and from the Danvers family.
steps.tip: Those three are invented, like everything else here.

steps.do: Scroll down to "Share a request". Leave both boxes empty and tap "Send to the prayer team".
steps.see: Nothing is sent. A short note says "Add a request first".

steps.do: Now send one properly. Put a made-up first name in the top box, write a made-up request in the second — something like "Please pray for my neighbour's new job" — tick "Keep it on my prayer list", and tap "Send to the prayer team".
steps.see: Your request appears on the wall with the name you typed and today's date. Nothing leaves the practice app. This is the part no tester has ever been able to try.

steps.do: Tap "I prayed" on one of the other requests.
steps.see: Say what it does and whether it is clear that this is private to you and does not tell anybody.

steps.do: Tap "Give" in the bar at the bottom, then tap "Give online now".
steps.see: Nothing happens — giving is switched off in the practice church. Say whether the screen made that clear BEFORE you tapped, or whether you expected something to happen.

steps.do: Tap "Events" in the bar at the bottom and look at the lists and the category buttons.
steps.see: Events with dates, and buttons like All, Kids, Students, Women, Men. Say whether anything about the way they are listed is confusing.

steps.do: Turn on Airplane Mode, then tap "Home" at the bottom.
steps.see: The Home screen still shows the latest message and the events. The app works with no signal.

steps.do: With Airplane Mode still on, open "📝 My notes on this message" again, type a second note — Pray for the Thursday trip — and tap "Add".
steps.see: The second note is added under the first, with no signal. Then close the panel with ✕ and turn Airplane Mode off.

steps.do: Tap "More" at the bottom, scroll to "Appearance" and choose "Dark".
steps.see: The whole screen turns dark straight away.

steps.do: Tap "Home" at the bottom.
steps.see: The Home screen is dark too, and still readable — nothing has disappeared into the background. Leave it dark — the challenge in part 3 will ask you to turn it back.

steps.do: Now the videos. This app has 3. Open each one and watch it right through, sound on: Explain it to me — https://jerrywins1.github.io/daraja-apps/shop/watch.html?app=church&mode=firsttime  Watch it work — https://jerrywins1.github.io/daraja-apps/shop/watch.html?app=church  Train me — https://jerrywins1.github.io/daraja-apps/shop/watch.html?app=church&mode=train
steps.see: Each one talks without stopping — no long silences, no sentence starting again. The screen behind the words changes to match what is being said, and when it points at something, that thing is really there. If a video talks about a button or a screen you did not see in this app, say so — that is a real fault and one of the most useful things you can find.
steps.tip: These videos were made for a real church that used to be in this test. If any of them still talks about a real church in America, or names a church that is not Grace Harbor, that is exactly the kind of thing we need to hear about.

steps.do: Last, the shop page everyone sees before they buy: https://jerrywins1.github.io/daraja-apps/shop/ — find this app on its shelf and read its card.
steps.see: The name and the one-line description match the app you just used. The price says Free, with an optional donation to Loving InDeed. That is right: nothing is sold, and nobody has to give. Nothing on the card promises something the app does not do. If the card and the app disagree, the card is the fault — say which bit. That is the end, thank you.
